figures.cap: plank of 9.6 m at 10 degrees to ground resting on a ramp inclined at 60 degrees; x along ramp

solutions.latex:
The angle in the triangle beside the ramp angle is supplementary: $180 - 60 = 120^\circ$.

Using the sine rule:
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 10^\circ} = \dfrac{9.6}{\sin 120^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{9.6 \sin 10^\circ}{\sin 120^\circ} \\ &\approx 1.9 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Sets up the sine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle with sides 28 cm, 22 cm, included angle 97 degrees, third side x

parts.latex:
In the triangle given below, calculate the length of $x$ correct to 1 decimal place.

\exfigure{719_q20_1}

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 28^2 + 22^2 - 2 \times 28 \times 22 \times \cos 97^\circ \\ x &= \sqrt{28^2 + 22^2 - 2 \times 28 \times 22 \times \cos 97^\circ} \\ &= 37.658\ldots \\ &\approx 37.7 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: boat at A and B, lighthouse L, bearings 62 and 44 degrees

solutions.latex:
In triangle $ABL$: $\angle LAB = 90^\circ-62^\circ = 28^\circ$ and $\angle ABL = 90^\circ+44^\circ = 134^\circ$, so
$$\angle ALB = 180^\circ - (28^\circ + 134^\circ) = 18^\circ$$
Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{LB}{\sin 28^\circ} = \dfrac{500}{\sin 18^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned}LB &= \dfrac{500\sin 28^\circ}{\sin 18^\circ} \\ &= 759.62\ldots \\ &\approx 760 \text{ m (to the nearest metre)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle ALB$ and sets up the sine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle with sides 5 and x, angles 105 and 20 degrees

parts.latex:
Which calculation could be used to find the value of $x$ in this triangle?

\exfigure{716_q4_1}

solutions.latex:
The side $x$ is opposite $105^\circ$ and the side $5$ is opposite $20^\circ$, so use the sine rule.

$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 105^\circ} = \dfrac{5}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

$$x = \dfrac{5 \times \sin 105^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

Hence the answer is option D.

figures.cap: triangle with sides 11 cm and x cm, angles 95 and 60

parts.latex: Calculate the value of $x$, correct to two significant figures.
Calculate the area of the triangle to the nearest square centimetre.

solutions.latex:
The angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$, so the third angle is
$$180^\circ-95^\circ-60^\circ=25^\circ$$
Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 60^\circ}=\dfrac{11}{\sin 25^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{11\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 25^\circ} \\ &= 23 \text{ cm (2 s.f.)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct rearranged expression for $x$, or equivalent merit
Correct application of the sine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula $A=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ with the included angle $95^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 11\times 22.54\ldots\times\sin 95^\circ \\ &= 123.5\ldots \\ &\approx 124 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct substitution into the area formula, or equivalent merit
